# Documents

## `__version__`

```python
__version__: str
```

The version string of the installed pyropdf package.

## `Document`

```python
Document(*, limits: DocumentLimits | None = None, version: str = '1.7')
```

A PDF document.

`open` opens an existing document, and `Document()` creates an
empty one. Documents are context managers that close on exit.

### `Document.limits`

```python
Document.limits: DocumentLimits
```

The limits that the document's operations start from.

### `Document.pages`

```python
Document.pages: Pages
```

The pages, a sequence of `Page` handles that edits keep valid.

### `Document.attachments`

```python
Document.attachments: Attachments
```

The embedded files, a mapping of `Attachment` handles by name.

### `Document.collection`

```python
Document.collection: Collection | None
```

The portable collection (`/Collection`), or `None`; assignable and deletable.

Assigning a `Collection` writes the schema, initial document,
view, sort order, colors, split settings, indirect `Navigator`,
and indirect `CollectionFolder` hierarchy in one transaction,
promoting the catalog's `/Version` to `1.7` or `2.0` as required.
`del doc.collection` removes `/Collection` and frees unreferenced
retired objects.

Settable.

### `Document.named_pages`

```python
Document.named_pages: NamedPages
```

The `/Names /Pages` name tree as a live `NamedPages` mutable mapping.

Assigning a mapping of `name -> Page | int` replaces the tree in one
transaction, and `del doc.named_pages` removes `/Names /Pages` and
frees retired `/Kids` nodes. Deleting or selecting pages in
`doc.pages` prunes entries naming removed pages in the same
transaction.

Settable.

### `Document.open_action`

```python
Document.open_action: Target | None
```

The catalog's `/OpenAction` destination or action, or `None` when absent.

Assigning writes a destination array or action dictionary in one
transaction, and `del doc.open_action` removes `/OpenAction`.

Settable.

### `Document.scripts`

```python
Document.scripts: DocumentScripts
```

The `/Names /JavaScript` name tree as a live `DocumentScripts` mutable mapping.

Assigning a mapping replaces the tree in one transaction, and
`del doc.scripts` removes `/Names /JavaScript` and frees retired
nodes. pyropdf never runs the scripts.

Settable.

### `Document.triggers`

```python
Document.triggers: DocumentTriggers
```

The catalog's `/AA` scripts as a live `DocumentTriggers` mutable mapping.

Assigning a mapping replaces `Catalog['AA']` in one transaction, and
`del doc.triggers` removes it.

Settable.

### `Document.objects`

```python
Document.objects: Objects
```

The indirect objects, a mapping by object number.

A locked encrypted document raises `EncryptedDocumentError`.

### `Document.destinations`

```python
Document.destinations: Destinations
```

The named destinations, a read-only mapping from name to `Destination`.

### `Document.form`

```python
Document.form: Form
```

The interactive form, a mapping from full field names to `Field` handles.

### `Document.outline`

```python
Document.outline: Outline
```

The outline (bookmarks) as its top-level items.

Assigning an iterable of `OutlineEntry` records replaces the
outline, and `del doc.outline` removes it; either frees the items
before that nothing else refers to.

Settable.

### `Document.structure`

```python
Document.structure: StructureTree
```

The logical structure tree as its top-level `StructureElement` handles.

Each element exposes its hierarchy, marked-content items, and
accessibility attributes, and `doc.structure.role_map` reads and
edits `/RoleMap`. `del doc.structure` removes `/StructTreeRoot`
and frees unreferenced structure objects in one transaction.

### `Document.threads`

```python
Document.threads: Threads
```

The article threads as a live `Threads` sequence.

Each `Thread` exposes its `Thread.beads` ring and its
information dictionary entries. `del doc.threads` removes
`/Threads` from the catalog, clears pages' `/B` bead arrays, and
frees unreferenced thread and bead objects in one transaction.

### `Document.fallback_fonts`

```python
Document.fallback_fonts: FallbackFonts
```

The fonts that render the CJK fonts that the document does not embed, by language.

hayro draws a font that a document does not embed in a Standard 14
font, which has no CJK glyphs, so such text renders blank. A
`FallbackFont` draws it instead: a font of the Adobe-Japan1,
Korea1, GB1, or CNS1 character collection takes the faces of
`"ja"`, `"ko"`, `"zh-CN"`, or `"zh-TW"`, and an
Adobe-Identity font those of the language that its name suggests,
such as MS-Gothic for `"ja"` or SimSun for `"zh-CN"`.

Until it is edited, the mapping holds the faces of the installed
font extras, `pyropdf[jp]`, `[ko]`, `[zh-cn]`, and
`[zh-tw]`, which rendering reads the first time that a page needs
them. Assigning a mapping of `FallbackFont` records replaces
every language, so `{}` renders without fallback fonts, and `del`
returns to the installed extras. The fonts belong to this
`Document` object and are not saved. Rendering uses them, and so
do what measures a rendering's glyphs: the exact boxes of text,
`exact_bboxes=True`, and the text runs of `Page.content`. Other
text extraction, which reads the character collection's Unicode, does
not.

Settable.

### `Document.trailer`

```python
Document.trailer: Dictionary
```

The trailer dictionary, which names the catalog as `/Root`.

### `Document.catalog`

```python
Document.catalog: Dictionary
```

The catalog, the indirect dictionary that the trailer's `/Root` names.

### `Document.transaction`

```python
Document.transaction(name: str = '') -> Transaction
```

Return a context manager that groups the edits of its block into one step named `name`.

### `Document.changes`

```python
Document.changes(*, incremental: bool) -> ChangeReport
```

Return what the edits since opening invalidate if the document is saved now.

The report identifies affected signature byte ranges and PDF/A or PDF/UA
claims. For an incremental save, `permissions` reports the signed
DocMDP and FieldMDP transforms' verdicts for the proposed edits.

### `Document.check`

```python
Document.check() -> StructuralReport
```

Return how the document departs from the Arlington PDF Model.

The check walks the current version from the trailer through the
model's object types and reports each value of the wrong type,
missing required key, key or value newer than the file's version,
value direct where it must be indirect or the reverse, and value
outside the key's possible values. It also reports the `invariant`
defects of page, name, number, and structure trees, references, and
appearance states, and the `profile` defects of a claimed PDF/A or
PDF/UA profile that need no rendering. Each defect names its object
and its clause. The walk runs under the document's limits.

### `Document.profiles`

```python
Document.profiles: Profiles
```

The PDF/A, PDF/UA, PDF/X, and PDF/VT claims of the XMP metadata, and the output intents.

The PDF/A name uses uppercase conformance, such as `"PDF/A-2B"`.
`pdfa_claim` gives its separate part and original conformance spelling.
The claims are what the document declares, not a validation. The
metadata read is capped at 16 MiB, beyond which `LimitError`
is raised with code `stream_data_size`.

### `Document.replace_image`

```python
Document.replace_image(xref: int, data: bytes)
```

Replace image object `xref` with JPEG, JPEG 2000, or PNG `data`, in one transaction.

The object keeps its number, so every page and form that paints it
paints the new image. JPEG and JPEG 2000 data is stored as it is;
PNG is decoded, its alpha written as a soft mask. The image's other
entries, such as `/Interpolate`, stay.

### `Document.remove_image`

```python
Document.remove_image(xref: int)
```

Make image object `xref` one transparent pixel, so that no placement shows it, in one transaction.

### `Document.rewrite_images`

```python
Document.rewrite_images(
    *,
    dpi_threshold: float | None = None,
    dpi_target: float | None = None,
    quality: int | None = None,
    lossy: bool = True,
    lossless: bool = True,
    bitonal: bool = True,
    color: bool = True,
    gray: bool = True,
    set_to_gray: bool = False,
    lossless_format: Literal['flate', 'jpeg', 'jpx'] = 'flate',
    bitonal_format: Literal['fax', 'fax-g3', 'fax-g3-2d', 'jbig2', 'flate'] = 'fax',
) -> ImageRewriteReport
```

Downsample and recompress the images that the pages place, each image object once, in one transaction.

An image whose resolution at its largest placement exceeds
`dpi_threshold` on either axis is resampled to `dpi_target` on
both, never gaining pixels, so an image placed on several pages
keeps the pixels that its largest placement needs. Resampling uses
`Pixmap.scale`'s filter, through premultiplied alpha.
`quality` (1 through 100) re-encodes every selected image even
when it keeps its size.

Lossy images (JPEG and JPEG 2000) are written as JPEG at
`quality`, or 75 when it is `None`. Lossless ones are written as
8-bit Flate, or as JPEG when `lossless_format` is `"jpeg"`. Choose
`"jpx"` for lossless JPEG 2000 output on gray and RGB XObjects.
Images that keep other sample spaces and inline images use Flate.
Bitonal images use Group 4 (`"fax"`), Group 3 one-dimensional
(`"fax-g3"`) or mixed (`"fax-g3-2d"`), lossless JBIG2 XObjects
(`"jbig2"`, 1-bit Flate for inline images), or 1-bit Flate (`"flate"`);
resampled bitonal pixels below half gray become black. A soft mask,
a stencil `/Mask` of the image's size, or a color-key mask
becomes a new 8-bit soft mask resampled with the image, so a mask
that other images share stays as it is. A mask of another size is
resampled at its own resolution by the image's placement and stays
a stencil `/Mask` (written as the bitonal format says) or a soft
mask; one that keeps its pixels stays as stored. A soft mask with
`/Matte` is un-premultiplied, and stencil mask images
(`/ImageMask`) are resampled as bitonal stencils.

DeviceGray and DeviceRGB images are rewritten from the colors that
hayro paints, with their `/Decode` arrays applied, and so is JPEG
2000 that names no color space, its own alpha (`/SMaskInData`)
becoming a soft mask. Images in DeviceCMYK, ICCBased, CalGray,
CalRGB, Lab, Separation, DeviceN, and Indexed keep their color space
and `/Decode` array: their stored samples, JPEG and JPEG 2000
decoded as hayro decodes them, are resampled channel by channel, and
a CMYK JPEG stays a CMYK JPEG, with an Adobe marker when its source
had one. Indexed images keep their bits and are resampled to the
nearest index, so that every color stays one of the palette's;
samples of 2 or 4 bits keep their depth, the resampled values
rounded to its levels, unless they become JPEG; 16-bit samples keep
their high 8 bits. Inline images are rewritten
too, by the placement that the `cm` operators give: those of a
page's own content make it one new stream, and a Form XObject or
annotation appearance that holds them is rewritten once, at their
largest drawing, as a new object that the pages draw, so whatever
else draws the original keeps it.

`lossy`, `lossless`, `bitonal`, `color`, and `gray` select
the kinds of image to rewrite. A selected image that a rewrite would
not keep stays as it is and is named in
`ImageRewriteReport.unsupported`: soft masks with `/Matte`
of another size, Indexed JPEG and JPEG 2000, other color spaces,
and inline images that the walk of content does not reach, as in
patterns.

`set_to_gray` converts the selected color images to DeviceGray,
and only images, where PyMuPDF's option of the same name converts
whole pages: `recolor` with `"gray"` converts the text,
vector graphics, and images of pages.

A rewrite is kept only when it saves at least 5% of the stored
data, its masks included, so repeating a call does not re-encode a
JPEG again. With none of `dpi_threshold`, `quality`, and
`set_to_gray` there is nothing to do, and the call returns zero
counts. A decoding failure raises and leaves the document as it
was; `history` can undo the step.

### `Document.recolor`

```python
Document.recolor(
    target: RecolorTarget,
    pages: Iterable[int] | None = None,
) -> RecolorReport
```

Convert the colors that `pages` paint to `target`, `"gray"`, `"rgb"`, or `"cmyk"`, as one step.

Every color operator of each page's content, of the Form XObjects
that it draws, and of its annotations' appearances becomes `g`,
`rg`, or `k` (and `G`, `RG`, `K`) in the target. Device,
CIE-based gray and RGB, and ICC-based spaces convert by their
component count, Indexed through its base, and Separation through
its alternate space when its tint transform is exponential, with
the conversions of ISO 32000-2 10.4.2: BT.601 luma for gray, and
full black generation for CMYK. Image objects and 8-bit inline
images convert too: a JPEG to a JPEG at the quality that its
quantization tables show, or Flate for CMYK, and others to 8-bit
Flate; their masks stay. The color arrays of annotations (`/C`,
`/IC`, and `/MK`'s `/BC` and `/BG`) convert as well.

Nothing is edited in place: a Form XObject, appearance, or image
that changes becomes a new object, so pages left out keep their
colors. Shadings, patterns, Lab, DeviceN, other tint transforms,
images whose masks read their samples, and Form XObjects nested
deeper than 16 or past 4,096 drawings are left as they are and
listed in `RecolorReport.unconverted`. `pages` holds page
indexes, negative ones from the end; it defaults to every page.

### `Document.layers`

```python
Document.layers: Layers
```

The optional content groups and configurations as a live `Layers` sequence.

`doc.layers.switch(xref, on=False)` hides a group and
`doc.layers.use(index)` applies a configuration of
`doc.layers.configs`; rendering and text extraction follow both.

### `Document.page_labels`

```python
Document.page_labels: list[PageLabelRange]
```

The page label ranges in page order, or `[]` without labels.

Each `PageLabelRange` labels the pages from its zero-based
`start` up to the next range; `page.label` gives one page's
label. Assigning a list replaces the ranges in one transaction, the
first of which must start at page 0, and `del doc.page_labels`
removes them. Inserting, moving, and deleting pages keeps each
page's label. Reads raise `LimitError` past 4,096 ranges or
kids, 32 levels, or 1 MiB of text; writes stop at 4,096 ranges and
1 MiB of prefixes (`page_label_input_size`).

Settable.

### `Document.metadata`

```python
Document.metadata: Metadata
```

The Info dictionary as a live `Metadata` mapping.

Assign a mapping to replace every entry in one transaction, or an
empty one to remove them. Edits write the matching properties of an
existing XMP packet too, so that the two stay equivalent.

Settable.

### `Document.xmp`

```python
Document.xmp: str | None
```

The catalog's XMP metadata packet as text, or `None` when absent.

The read is capped at 1 MiB, beyond which `LimitError` is
raised with code `stream_data_size`; read a larger packet through
`doc.catalog["Metadata"].read(max_size=...)`. Assigning a string
writes it unfiltered, into the existing stream or a new one, and
`del doc.xmp` removes the catalog's entry. Assigning a packet does
not change `metadata`.

Settable.

### `Document.pdfa_claim`

```python
Document.pdfa_claim: tuple[int, str] | None
```

The PDF/A part and the conformance spelling in XMP, such as `(2, "b")`, or `None`.

A declared part with no conformance gives an empty string. For the normalized
profile name, the other declarations, and the output intents, read `profiles`.

### `Document.page_mode`

```python
Document.page_mode: PageMode
```

How a viewer opens the document; unset or unknown reads as `PageMode.USE_NONE`.

Assign a `PageMode` or its PDF name string (ISO 32000-2 Table
29) in one transaction, or `del doc.page_mode` to remove
`/PageMode`.

Settable.

### `Document.page_layout`

```python
Document.page_layout: PageLayout
```

How a viewer lays pages out; unset or unknown reads as `PageLayout.SINGLE_PAGE`.

Assign a `PageLayout` or its PDF name string (ISO 32000-2 Table
29) in one transaction, or `del doc.page_layout` to remove
`/PageLayout`.

Settable.

### `Document.language`

```python
Document.language: str | None
```

The catalog's `/Lang` language tag as stored, or `None`.

The complete BCP 47 tag is kept, such as `"zh-TW"` or
`"sr-Latn-RS"`. Assigning writes a well-formed tag (ISO 32000-2
section 14.9.2.2) of at most 256 ASCII bytes, hyphen-separated subtags
of one to eight ASCII letters or digits, the first of letters only; a
non-string raises `TypeError` and a malformed tag raises
`PdfError`. `del doc.language` removes `/Lang`.

Settable.

### `Document.mark_info`

```python
Document.mark_info: MarkInfo | None
```

The catalog's `/MarkInfo` flags, or `None` without a `/MarkInfo` dictionary.

Each flag is `True` only when the dictionary holds `true`.
Assigning a `MarkInfo` writes all three flags in one
transaction, and `del doc.mark_info` removes `/MarkInfo`.

Settable.

### `Document.viewer_preferences`

```python
Document.viewer_preferences: ViewerPreferences | None
```

The catalog's `/ViewerPreferences`, or `None` without the dictionary.

Entries of the wrong type or of unknown values read as `None`.
Assigning a `ViewerPreferences` replaces the dictionary with
the fields that are not `None` in one transaction, keeping an
indirect dictionary's object number when it already has one, and
`del doc.viewer_preferences` removes `/ViewerPreferences`.

Settable.

### `Document.requirements`

```python
Document.requirements: tuple[DocumentRequirement, ...]
```

The catalog's viewer capability requirements (`/Requirements`).

Assigning an iterable of `DocumentRequirement` records replaces
`Catalog['Requirements']` in one transaction (promoting the catalog
version to `1.7` for `RequirementType.ENABLE_JAVASCRIPTS` alone
or `2.0` with a trailer `/ID` when PDF 2.0 requirement types,
penalties, or versions are present, or removing `/Requirements` when
empty) and frees unreferenced retired objects; `del doc.requirements`
removes `/Requirements` and frees unreferenced objects.

Settable.

### `Document.history`

```python
Document.history: History
```

The steps that undo and redo walk.

### `Document.revisions`

```python
Document.revisions: tuple[Revision, ...]
```

The incremental file revisions of the opened document, oldest first.

Each `Revision` gives its zero-based `index` (matching
`Signature.revision`), its `end` offset, and the indirect
object numbers that it `added`, `updated`, or `freed`, and
`Revision.open` opens that revision as an independent
`Document` sharing the file's bytes. An empty in-memory
document or one whose cross-reference index was repaired returns
`()`, and unsaved edits in memory do not change the revisions.

### `Document.is_closed`

```python
Document.is_closed: bool
```

Whether `close` was called.

### `Document.is_repaired`

```python
Document.is_repaired: bool
```

Whether opening recovered damaged cross-reference data.

### `Document.is_linearized`

```python
Document.is_linearized: bool
```

Whether the opened file is linearized for fast web view (ISO 32000-2 Annex F).

The file's first object, in its first 1024 bytes, is a linearization
dictionary whose `/L` is the file's length. An update appended to
a linearized file changes its length, so such a file reads as not
linearized. Edits in memory do not change the answer; a document
without a file is not linearized.

### `Document.needs_password`

```python
Document.needs_password: bool
```

Whether the document is locked until `unlock` receives its password.

### `Document.access`

```python
Document.access: Access | None
```

What opened an unlocked encrypted document, or `None` for a locked one.

An unencrypted document grants `Access.OWNER`.

### `Document.encryption_method`

```python
Document.encryption_method: str | None
```

The security handler of an unlocked encrypted document, such as `"Standard V5 R6 256-bit AES"`.

`None` for an unencrypted or locked document.

### `Document.permissions`

```python
Document.permissions: Permissions
```

What the document permits, as `Permissions` flags.

A locked document permits nothing. An unencrypted document, or one
unlocked with its owner password, permits everything. Otherwise the
flags are those that the encryption grants the user password.

### `Document.unlock`

```python
Document.unlock(password: str | RecipientCredential) -> Access
```

Unlock with a password or a `RecipientCredential` and return its access.

The owner password grants `Access.OWNER` and the user password
`Access.USER`; a password that matches neither raises
`PasswordError`. An unencrypted document grants
`Access.OWNER` to any password. Unlocking a locked document
reads it again, which starts its history over; unlocking an unlocked
one only checks the password, and keeps the history. Passwords are
capped at 127 UTF-8 bytes.

### `Document.save`

```python
Document.save(
    path: str | os.PathLike[str],
    /,
    *,
    incremental: bool = False,
    encryption: Encryption | RecipientEncryption | None = None,
    prune: bool = False,
    compress: bool = False,
    compression_level: int = 6,
    decompress: bool = False,
    keep_id: bool = False,
    cross_reference: Literal['table', 'stream', 'hybrid'] | None = None,
    object_streams: bool = False,
    renumber: bool = False,
    dedupe: bool = False,
    linearize: bool = False,
)
```

Write the document to a file.

The document is written completely to a new file beside `path`,
which then replaces `path` atomically, keeping an existing file's
permissions; a final symlink is followed and kept. A failed save
leaves `path` as it was. `incremental=True` appends only what
changed to the bytes of the opened file, so that a save without
edits reproduces it byte for byte; a full save rewrites every object
and keeps the values of untouched ones.

Without `encryption`, a full save writes an encrypted document
decrypted and an incremental save keeps its encryption;
`Encryption.KEEP` keeps it in a full save too, copying its
untouched encrypted bytes, and an `Encryption` encrypts a full
save anew.

`prune=True` writes only the objects that the trailer reaches, so
what an edit unlinked leaves the file; the document in memory keeps
them. An incremental save keeps the objects of the opened file, so
it refuses `prune`.

`compress=True` compresses with Flate, at zlib's
`compression_level` from 0 through 9, each stream that has no
filter, where that makes it shorter; XMP metadata stays unfiltered.
`decompress=True` removes the filters that hayro-syntax decodes,
keeping image filters such as `DCTDecode`, and excludes
`compress`. An incremental save compresses only the streams that
it writes and refuses `decompress`. An encrypted save compresses
before it encrypts. The document in memory keeps its streams.

A save of an edited document keeps the first element of the
trailer's `/ID` and renews the second, and a full save, or an
incremental save of edits, gives a document without `/ID` a new
one (ISO 32000-2 section 14.4). The new element is the MD5 digest
of the bytes before it, so the same document saves to the same
bytes. A save without edits writes `/ID` as read, and so does any
save with `keep_id=True`. Encryption keys derive from the first
element, which a save keeps.

`cross_reference` writes the cross-reference data as a `"table"`
or as a `"stream"` (PDF 1.5); `None` keeps the form of the
section that the opened file's `startxref` names, and writes a
table for a hybrid-reference file or a document without a file.
`cross_reference="hybrid"` writes a complete classic table and
a supplemental cross-reference stream in a subsequent section.
When packing is requested it keeps objects reachable from the
trailer visible to readers that only understand the classic table.
An edited incremental save of a hybrid appends a new hybrid section.

In a pure cross-reference stream, `object_streams=True` packs
every object that ISO 32000-2 section
7.5.7 lets an object stream hold into object streams of up to 100
objects: those that are not streams, have generation 0, and are not
the encryption dictionary. It writes a cross-reference stream, so
it excludes `cross_reference="table"`. Both raise the header's
version to 1.5 when it is lower. The streams that a save adds are
compressed with Flate at `compression_level` unless
`decompress`, and an encrypted save encrypts each object stream
as a whole. An incremental save keeps the form of the opened file,
so it refuses both.

`renumber=True` numbers the objects that a full save writes 1, 2,
3, and so on in the order of their numbers, with generation 0, and
the objects that it adds after them; each reference follows its
object, and a reference to an object that the save does not write
becomes null. An encrypted save encrypts each object with the key
of its new number. The document in memory keeps its numbers, and an
incremental save, which keeps the opened file's, refuses it.

`dedupe=True` merges each set of identical objects into the one
with the smallest number and points every reference to it; streams
merge when their dictionaries and data are identical. Pages,
annotations, form fields, structure elements, outline items,
optional-content groups, the objects that the trailer names, and
objects in cycles of references never merge. It needs
`prune=True`, and so a full save. The document in memory keeps its
objects.

`linearize=True` writes the file linearized for fast web view
(ISO 32000-2 Annex F): the first page's objects, then a hint stream
and the other pages' objects in page order, so that a viewer shows
the first page before the rest arrives. It writes the objects that
the pages, the trailer, and the catalog reach, numbered anew, so it
prunes and renumbers whatever `prune` and `renumber` say, and
moves the attributes that pages inherit from the page tree into the
pages. It writes a cross-reference table, so it refuses
`cross_reference="stream"` or `"hybrid"`, `object_streams`, and `dedupe`,
and an incremental save refuses it. `is_linearized` reads
whether an opened file is linearized.

### `Document.to_bytes`

```python
Document.to_bytes(
    *,
    incremental: bool = False,
    encryption: Encryption | RecipientEncryption | None = None,
    max_size: int | None = 536870912,
    prune: bool = False,
    compress: bool = False,
    compression_level: int = 6,
    decompress: bool = False,
    keep_id: bool = False,
    cross_reference: Literal['table', 'stream', 'hybrid'] | None = None,
    object_streams: bool = False,
    renumber: bool = False,
    dedupe: bool = False,
    linearize: bool = False,
) -> bytes
```

Return the document as PDF bytes, as `save` writes them with the same options.

`max_size` bounds the output, 512 MiB by default, and refuses the
write that would pass it with `LimitError` code
`pdf_output_size`; `None` leaves it unbounded for trusted input.

### `Document.signatures`

```python
Document.signatures: list[Signature]
```

The signed signature fields of the opened file, in field order.

Each `Signature` verifies against the bytes that the document
was opened from: edits since then are not part of any revision.

### `Document.certification`

```python
Document.certification: DocMdpPermission | None
```

The author certification permission from `Catalog['Perms']['DocMDP']`, or `None`.

### `Document.security_store`

```python
Document.security_store: SecurityStore | None
```

The Document Security Store `Catalog['DSS']` (PDF 2.0), or `None`; `del` removes it.

Assigning a `SecurityStore` writes DER certificates, OCSP
responses, CRLs, and per-signature `/VRI` entries as deduplicated
indirect Flate streams in one transaction, keeping earlier signatures
intact across `save(incremental=True)`.

Settable.

### `Document.legal_attestation`

```python
Document.legal_attestation: LegalAttestation | None
```

`Catalog['Legal']` (PDF 1.5), or `None` when absent; `del` removes it.

Settable.

### `Document.encrypted_payload`

```python
Document.encrypted_payload: EncryptedPayload | None
```

The encrypted file selected by a PDF 2.0 unencrypted wrapper (§7.6.7).

Return `None` when the hidden collection, embedded-file tree and catalog
association do not identify the same encrypted payload. Malformed filter
metadata or a missing stream on an identified payload raises
`MalformedPdfError`.

### `Document.prepare_signature`

```python
Document.prepare_signature(
    field: str,
    *,
    doc_mdp: DocMdpPermission | None = None,
    field_lock: FieldLock | None = None,
    is_timestamp: bool = False,
    reason: str | None = None,
    location: str | None = None,
    contact: str | None = None,
    reserve: int = 16384,
) -> int
```

Prepare an unsigned signature field for an external signer in one transaction and return its `xref`.

Creates an invisible signature field `field` on the first page when
none exists, writes `/Lock` for `field_lock` and `/SV` seed values
for `doc_mdp`, `is_timestamp`, and `reason`, and returns the field
dictionary's object number so external signers such as pyHanko (or a
subsequent `sign` call) can fill it cleanly.

### `Document.sign`

```python
Document.sign(
    field: str,
    signer: Signer,
    *,
    timestamper: Timestamper | None = None,
    doc_mdp: DocMdpPermission | None = None,
    field_lock: FieldLock | None = None,
    reason: str | None = None,
    location: str | None = None,
    contact: str | None = None,
    reserve: int = 16384,
) -> bytes
```

Sign the document as PAdES B-B, or B-T with `timestamper`, in a new revision, and return its bytes.

`field` names an unsigned signature field, or a new invisible one
on the first page. The signature dictionary, the field, and any
unsaved edits are saved incrementally after the opened file's bytes,
so earlier signatures stay intact, and the CMS signature of
`signer` covers every byte but its own (ETSI EN 319 142-1). The
signature dictionary's `/M` is the current time, and `reason`,
`location`, and `contact` become `/Reason`, `/Location`, and
`/ContactInfo`. `doc_mdp` certifies an unsigned document with a
`DocMDP` transform and `Catalog['Perms']['DocMDP']`, and
`field_lock` records a `FieldMDP` transform.

`timestamper` receives the digest of the signature value and the
name of its hash algorithm, and returns an RFC 3161 time-stamp token
over that digest; pyropdf makes no network access. A token that
does not stamp the signature raises `ValueError`.

`reserve` is the bytes kept for the CMS signature, 16 KiB by
default; a signature that needs more raises `ValueError`.
Afterwards the document reads the signed revision, so that
`save(path, incremental=True)` writes the returned bytes, and its
undo history starts anew. A failure leaves the document as it was.

Signing runs as one transaction, which other threads' edits wait
for. Signing inside a transaction raises `PdfError`, as does
a callback that edits the document. An encrypted document raises
`ValueError`.

### `Document.timestamp`

```python
Document.timestamp(
    timestamper: Timestamper,
    *,
    field: str = 'DocTimeStamp',
    reserve: int = 16384,
) -> bytes
```

Append an RFC 3161 `/DocTimeStamp` revision to the document and return its bytes (ISO 32000-2 §12.8.5).

`timestamper` receives the SHA-256 digest of the signed byte ranges
and `"sha256"`, and returns the DER of an RFC 3161 `TimeStampToken`
stamping that digest; pyropdf makes no network access. Afterwards the
document reads the timestamped revision and earlier signatures remain
intact.

### `Document.render`

```python
Document.render(
    pages: Iterable[int] | None = None,
    *,
    dpi: float | None = None,
    matrix: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    fit: int | tuple[int, int] | None = None,
    alpha: bool = False,
    background: tuple[int, int, int] | tuple[int, int, int, int] | None = None,
    annotations: bool = True,
    colorspace: Colorspace | Literal['gray', 'rgb'] = Colorspace.RGB,
    hinting: bool = False,
    glyph_cache: bool = False,
    format: Literal['png', 'jpeg'] = 'png',
    quality: int = 95,
    workers: int | None = None,
    max_size: int | None = 536870912,
) -> list[bytes]
```

Render pages of the current version to encoded images, in the order of `pages`.

`dpi`, `matrix`, `fit`, `alpha`, `background`,
`annotations`, `colorspace`, `hinting`, and `glyph_cache` mean
what they mean to `Page.pixmap`, so the default is opaque RGB at
72 dpi, `fit` scales each page individually from its own display
size, and each image is what
`page.pixmap(...).to_bytes(format, quality=quality)` returns.
`format` is `"png"` or `"jpeg"` at `quality`, 1 through 100;
JPEG has no alpha. `pages` holds page indexes, negative ones from
the end, and may repeat them; it defaults to every page, and may
hold up to the larger of the page count and 4,096 entries, past
which `LimitError` code `page_entry_count` refuses it.

Every page renders from the one version that is current when the
call starts, so commits from other threads leave the batch as it
was. The pages render on up to `workers` threads, 1 through 64,
and up to four CPUs by default, with the GIL released; the threads
are fewer when their largest rasters would hold more than about
512 MB at once. With `glyph_cache=True`, each thread keeps the
glyphs that it rasterized, outside `DocumentLimits`, until the
call returns. `max_size` bounds the encoded bytes of all the
images together, 512 MiB by default, with `LimitError` code
`render_output_size`; `None` leaves it unbounded.

### `Document.text`

```python
Document.text(
    pages: Iterable[int] | None = None,
    *,
    clip: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    clipped: bool = False,
    ligatures: bool = True,
    whitespace: bool = True,
    dehyphenate: bool = False,
    unmapped: Unmapped = 'skip',
    max_glyphs: int | None = 262144,
    max_size: int | None = 67108864,
) -> str
```

Return the text of the given pages of the current version, joined in their order.

`pages` holds zero-based page indexes, negative ones counted from
the end and repeats allowed; `None` means every page. It may hold
up to the larger of the page count and 4,096 entries, past which
`LimitError` code `page_entry_count` refuses it. The text
equals joining `Page.text` of each page with the same options,
read from one version even while other threads edit the document.
`max_glyphs` bounds each page and `max_size` the whole text. The
GIL is released while hayro interprets the pages.

### `Document.markdown`

```python
Document.markdown(
    pages: Iterable[int] | None = None,
    *,
    table_strategy: Literal['lines', 'text'] | None = 'lines',
    max_size: int | None = 67108864,
) -> str
```

Return the given pages of the current version as Markdown, joined in their order.

Page selection and extraction use one version even while another thread edits the document.

Headings come from font sizes: the size that holds the most text is
the body's, and larger sizes map in descending order to `#`
through `####`. Wrapped CJK lines join without spaces, leading
bullets and `1.` or `1)` become Markdown lists, and the bold and
italic of embedded fonts become emphasis. Multicolumn text follows
its gutters, and vertical CJK columns read top to bottom and right to
left; ruby and mixed orientations are not interpreted.

Complete bordered tables of `Page.tables` become Markdown
tables in reading order; `table_strategy="text"` adds the
borderless tables that overlap none of them, and `None` converts no
table. `pages` is as for `text`. More than `max_size` bytes
of UTF-8 in all raise `LimitError` with code
`markdown_output_size` without a partial result;
`max_size=None` lifts the limit.

### `Document.to_json`

```python
Document.to_json(
    pages: Iterable[int] | None = None,
    *,
    table_strategy: Literal['lines', 'text'] | None = 'lines',
    max_size: int | None = 67108864,
) -> str
```

Return the given pages of the current version as JSON: each page's size and its elements.

Page selection and extraction use one version even while another thread edits the document.

The document is `{"pages": [...]}`, each page `{"index",
"width", "height", "elements"}`, and each element as
`Element.to_dict` gives it: a heading, paragraph, list item,
table, or image in reading order with its page index and its box in
display space. Headings, lists, and tables are found as
`markdown` finds them, and `pages` and `table_strategy`
are as for it. More than `max_size` bytes of UTF-8 element text
raise `LimitError` with code `export_output_size` without a
partial result; `max_size=None` lifts the limit.

### `Document.to_chunks`

```python
Document.to_chunks(
    pages: Iterable[int] | None = None,
    *,
    max_chars: int = 2000,
    table_strategy: Literal['lines', 'text'] | None = 'lines',
    max_size: int | None = 67108864,
) -> list[Chunk]
```

Return the elements of `to_json` grouped into retrieval chunks of at most `max_chars` characters.

Page selection and extraction use one version even while another thread edits the document.

A chunk is a run of consecutive elements joined as Markdown, headings
marked with `#`; each heading starts a chunk, and
`Chunk.section` names the headings above it. A paragraph or
list item longer than `max_chars` is split at white space, its
pieces keeping its page and box; a table, image, or heading is never
split, and a chunk of one that is longer is
`Chunk.oversized`. Every element keeps its page index and box,
and `Chunk.to_dict` gives JSON-safe values. `pages`,
`table_strategy`, and `max_size` are as for `to_json`.

### `Document.flatten`

```python
Document.flatten(*, annotations: bool = True, widgets: bool = True)
```

Draw annotation and widget appearances into page content and take them off their pages.

`annotations` covers every annotation but links, which stay, and
takes popups off with them; `widgets` covers form widgets and
removes the interactive form. Each one is drawn as rendering shows
it: its normal appearance mapped onto its rectangle, or the
appearance that rendering draws for one stored without, and hidden
ones leave undrawn. A widget without an appearance draws nothing;
fill fields first, which draws them. The edit is one step.

### `Document.sanitize`

```python
Document.sanitize(
    path: str | os.PathLike[str],
    /,
    *,
    javascript: bool = True,
    actions: bool = True,
    attachments: bool = True,
    metadata: bool = True,
    comments: bool = True,
    hidden_text: bool = True,
    unused: bool = True,
) -> SanitizeReport
```

Remove hidden or active content in one transaction and save the document in full to `path`.

`javascript` removes every action whose `/Next` chain runs
JavaScript and the document's JavaScript name tree; `actions`
removes every action: `/A`, `/OpenAction`, and `/AA`, while
links keep their `/Dest` destinations. `attachments` removes
the embedded file name tree, portfolios, `/AF` associations, and
file attachment annotations. `metadata` removes the Info
dictionary and every `/Metadata` and `/PieceInfo`. `comments`
removes markup annotations and their pop-ups, keeping links and
widgets. `hidden_text` removes text shown in rendering mode 3, as
OCR layers are, from page content and from the form XObjects that
pages and appearances paint, each with the mode it is painted in; a
form painted both invisibly and visibly keeps the text that it
does not hide itself. `unused` writes only the objects that the
trailer reaches.

The save is never incremental, so the file has one revision. The
returned `SanitizeReport` counts what each kind removed and
reports, as `changes` does before the save, the signatures
and profile claims that the result breaks, and the claims that it
no longer makes, as removing the XMP metadata drops them. The
document in memory
keeps the edits, which `history` can undo.

### `Document.subset_fonts`

```python
Document.subset_fonts() -> tuple[SubsetFont, ...]
```

Subset each embedded TrueType, OpenType, and CFF program to the glyphs that the pages draw, as one step.

The glyphs are those that rendering draws with every optional
content group on, with the glyphs that they draw as composite
components or `seac` accents. A subset keeps every glyph ID and
empties the outlines of the others, so text, encodings, widths, and
ToUnicode are unchanged; the font names gain a subset tag. Programs
that annotation appearances or the form's default resources reach,
and Type 1 and Type 3 fonts, stay whole. Returns the programs that
shrank; `history` can undo the step.

### `Document.font_program`

```python
Document.font_program(font: int | FontInfo) -> FontProgram | None
```

Return the embedded program of a font, by its object number or a `FontInfo` from `page.fonts()`.

The program is the decoded `FontFile`, `FontFile2`, or
`FontFile3` stream of the font's descriptor, or of a `Type0`
font's descendant font; `None` when the font embeds none, as Type 3
fonts and the standard 14 fonts do. A value that is not a font
dictionary, or a `FontInfo` of another document, raises
`ValueError`.

### `Document.close`

```python
Document.close()
```

Close the document and release its data; later operations raise `DocumentClosedError`.

### `Document.__enter__`

```python
Document.__enter__() -> Self
```

Enter a context manager and return this document.

### `Document.__exit__`

```python
Document.__exit__(
    exc_type: type[BaseException] | None,
    exc_value: BaseException | None,
    traceback: TracebackType | None,
)
```

Close the document when leaving a context manager.

## `open`

```python
open(
    source: str | os.PathLike[str] | bytes | bytearray | memoryview,
    /,
    *,
    password: str | None = None,
    credential: RecipientCredential | None = None,
    limits: DocumentLimits | None = None,
) -> Document
```

Open a PDF from a file path or from the bytes of a document.

A document with an empty user password decrypts on its own; any other
encrypted document needs `password`, or `Document.unlock` after
opening, and refuses to read its objects until then. A wrong password
raises `PasswordError`. Passwords are capped at 127 UTF-8 bytes.

Use `credential` for an RSA recipient-encrypted PDF.

Opening reads the cross-reference data only; `bytes` are read in place,
without a copy, and other buffers are copied. `limits` bounds the work,
and `DocumentLimits.web` also reads every object at open. Input that is not a readable PDF, including empty
input, raises `MalformedPdfError`, and a missing file raises
`FileNotFoundError`.

## `Probe`

```python
Probe(
    *,
    page_count: int,
    version: str,
    needs_password: bool,
    is_repaired: bool,
    metadata: Mapping[str, str],
)
```

What `probe` reads without loading the whole document.

## `probe`

```python
probe(
    source: str | os.PathLike[str] | bytes | bytearray | memoryview,
    /,
    *,
    password: str | None = None,
    credential: RecipientCredential | None = None,
    max_file_size: int | None = None,
) -> Probe
```

Read the page count, version, encryption, and metadata without loading the whole document.

Use `credential` for a recipient-encrypted PDF. This suits scanning many files.
`max_file_size` refuses larger input
before parsing with `LimitError` code `file_size`; `None`, the
default, leaves it unbounded. The metadata text is capped at 1 MiB, and
passwords at 127 UTF-8 bytes; a wrong password raises `PasswordError`.
